model: Bank FCFE distributable earnings at cost of equity with residual income on tangible book cross-check (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bvps_5yr_cagr (FY2019 22.75 -> FY2024 26.04). Per-share book is the bank measure: buybacks shrink total equity (equity_5yr 1.1%), so total-equity CAGR understates per-share compounding.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR (3yr 108%, 5yr 32.5%) diverges massively from equity/BVPS CAGR. EPS is recovering from a depressed FY2020-21 base (FY2020 loss of EUR -2.33/sh, FY2021 EUR 0.23) under the 2022-24 rate cycle; it is not a sustainable growth rate. Revenue (total income) 3yr 9.5% is also rate-cycle inflated: NII went from 4.8bn (FY2021) to 8.3bn (FY2024) and is now flat to slightly down (9M25 -1.2% YoY).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null on purpose. Bank operating cash flow is balance-sheet noise (deposit and trading flows), and Metrics.csv carries no OCF/capex for CBK.DE. Revenue = total income. Periods FY2019/FY2021/FY2024 from metrics_normalized.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone value. Commerzbank keeps executing Momentum (3,900 roles cut by 2028, fee growth, cost-income towards 52%), reaches about 13% Net RoTE by FY2028 (2pt below target) and keeps a 100% payout. At a 10.75% CoE (including the control-overhang premium) that is worth about 1.3x tangible book, below the market's about 1.45x: today's price already discounts slightly more than a haircut Momentum.
scenario_narratives.bull: Momentum targets met (15% Net RoTE FY2028, about EUR 4.4bn net income ex-AT1). The value of that plan is what a control buyer has to pay. UniCredit (about 47.6% combined after the June-2026 exchange offer at 0.485 UCG per share, about EUR 30.8 implied then) would need a domination agreement, merger or squeeze-out at IDW S1 compensation on these plan figures, or a sweetened offer, to take out the rest. The ECB decision on UniCredit's >30% application was expected around October 2026.
scenario_narratives.bear: German credit cycle and rate cuts stall RoTE about 10% (below CoE). The worst minority outcome: UniCredit reaches control through market purchases without a premium bid, capital returns slow, and the stock de-rates below tangible book. Berlin's opposition (Finanzagentur about 12%) delays the deal without stopping it, so the overhang lasts.

takeover_situation.stake: about 47.6% combined (direct shares plus derivatives and tendered shares) as of July 2026, per Analysis.json. Voting rights were about 26% in August 2025 (Q3-2025 interim, voting-rights notification of 25 Aug 2025).
takeover_situation.offer_history: Voluntary public exchange offer of 0.485 UniCredit shares per Commerzbank share (about EUR 30.8 implied); acceptance period closed June 2026. BaFin cleared the >30% mandatory-offer threshold in March 2026.
takeover_situation.pending: ECB decision on UniCredit's application to go above 30%, expected about October 2026 and not confirmed at the valuation date.
takeover_situation.opposition: German Federal Government via Finanzagentur (about 12%) rejected the offer as lacking an adequate premium. Chancellor Merz (July 2026) said Berlin would not block it. Management (CEO Orlopp) favours independence.
takeover_situation.valuation_implication: The current price (EUR 36.27) is about 18% above the June-2026 offer's implied value. The market is pricing standalone execution plus some chance of a better control price, not the old offer terms. A German domination agreement or squeeze-out would set minority compensation at the higher of the 3-month VWAP and an IDW S1 capitalised-earnings value, which works as a soft floor once UniCredit seeks full control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Commerzbank is valued as a standalone bank on the flow it actually distributes: net income to ordinary shareholders after AT1 coupons and NCI, less the equity retained to fund RWA growth at a 13.5% CET1 target. That FCFE is discounted at a 10% EUR cost of equity, with no net debt deducted. Deposits and debt securities are bank funding, not leverage to subtract. The UniCredit situation is framed, not forecast. Base = standalone value, which a control buyer would also have to recognise. Bull = Momentum targets delivered, approximating the compensation a domination agreement, merger or squeeze-out would have to clear. Bear = creeping control without a premium plus a credit downturn. The model never adds a takeover premium on top of fundamental value: the last offer (June 2026) was struck below today's price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Stale anchors: the latest extracted filing is Q3-2025 (30 Sep 2025). FY2025, Q1/H1-2026 actuals and the Q3-2026 release (early Nov 2026) can move base-year earnings, share count and tangible book. Re-run once they are extracted.
Share count of 1,095m is estimated, not filed (1,125m at Sep-25 less the about EUR 1bn buyback to Feb-2026). Any further 2026 buyback or cancellation changes the divisor.

FY2026 guidance in Analysis.json (about EUR 4.2bn net profit, about 16% RoTE) is unverified and probably conflated with the 2028 target. If it is real, the base case is too low by roughly EUR 4-6/share.
ECB rate path: NII is about 60% of income. Faster cuts or a flatter curve compress margins faster than the structural hedge offsets.
German SME/export credit cycle and mBank CHF-mortgage litigation: the risk result can double in a downturn (FY2020: EUR 1.75bn).
UniCredit control outcomes cut both ways: a squeeze-out or domination agreement at a premium (upside), or control without a premium and a reduced payout (downside).
Valuation is terminal-heavy (about half of value): Gordon at CoE 10.75% and g 2.4% is about 12.3x terminal FCFE. A 1pt change in CoE moves the base case about 10-13%.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: The 2026-10-25 multiples sanity check tripped on implied P/B 1.41x against a 10yr maximum of 0.72x (FY2024). One fix pass was applied: +0.75pt CoE premium for the UniCredit control overhang and residual cyclicality, and growth after FY2028 plus terminal growth capped at the 2.4% through-cycle CAGR. Weighted IV fell from EUR 36.25 to EUR 31.87, implied P/B about 1.18x. The check still trips, and the valuation is kept there on purpose rather than forced into the band, for three reasons. (1) The band cannot be cleared without valuing the bank below what its own earnings support. A pass needs an IV below about EUR 29 (1.08x book). At the fixed 10.75% CoE, that is only justified by RoTE below about 11%, close to the bear case, while Commerzbank earned about 10% underlying on TTM Sep-2025 and guides to 15% by 2028. (2) The FY2016-24 P/B band (0.23-0.72x) was set when RoTE was 0-8%: FY2020 was a loss. Justified P/TBV = (RoTE - g)/(CoE - g), so the band measured a sub-CoE bank. It is not a ceiling on a bank earning around its cost of equity. (3) The window ends at FY2024 because FY2025 and later filings are not extracted. The 2025 re-rating (stock about EUR 18.7 to EUR 30-43 on UniCredit's approach and the Momentum upgrade) is outside the data the check can see. The P/B gap is a structural re-rating plus takeover overhang, not a WACC or growth error. The investment conclusion is the same either way: the stock trades about 14% above the probability-weighted value and about 70% above the 15%-hurdle entry price. It is a hold-or-avoid, not a buy, unless a control premium crystallises.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (CBK.DE, EUR) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 29.32-43.37.
data_sources.financials: CBK.DE_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2014-9M2025) and kpis (NetIncomeInclAT1, CET1Ratio, BookValuePerShare, CreditImpairmentCharge, NII, fees). Q3-2025 interim (CBK.DE_Quarterly_Q3-2025.txt): income statement, restructuring, intangible assets, buyback, share count. FY2024 annual: profit attributable 2,465 and AT1-coupon deduction basis.
data_sources.qualitative: CBK.DE_Analysis.json (UniCredit takeover timeline, Momentum targets, 2026 guidance; the 2026 items are not verified against a filing).

residual_income_crosscheck.method: Justified P/TBV = (steady-state RoTE - g) / (CoE - g), times tangible book per share. Tangible book is about EUR 27.5bn after the EUR 1bn buyback, on 1,095m shares = about EUR 25.1/share.
residual_income_crosscheck.conclusion: After the 2026-10-25 fix (CoE +0.75pt, growth capped at 2.4%) the FCFE engine values sit 0-7% above the steady-state residual-income values: base 32.42 vs 31.9, bull 40.53 vs 40.3, bear 22.12 vs 20.6. The gap is the FY2026-28 earnings ramp funded by excess CET1, which the single-stage formula leaves out. The two methods agree. The market price is about 1.45x TBV. At a 10.75% CoE and 2.4% g that implies about 14.5% sustainable RoTE, close to the full 15% Momentum target, against the base case's 13%.

prior_version.note: Same-day build before the sanity-check fix pass. Anchors (price, balance sheet, shares, guidance) unchanged.

Methodology: +0.75pt CoE premium (control overhang +0.5, cyclicality +0.25) in all scenarios
Driver change: years 4-10 and terminal growth capped at the 2.4% through-cycle CAGR
bridge.note: Mostly bull (terminal g 3.0 -> 2.4, years 4-7 at 3-5% -> 2.4): 44.45 -> 40.53. Base 33.42 -> 32.42. Bear about unchanged.

reconciliation.unchanged: Scenario weights (25/50/25), FY2026-28 earnings ramp (years 1-3), retention path, base-year earnings, share count and terminal_cap_multiple are left as they were. The FY2025 annual or the 2026 interims would move the ramp and the anchors: verified FY2026 guidance near EUR 4.2bn would lift base by about EUR 4-6. An ECB decision on UniCredit would move the weights and the control-overhang premium.

inputs.sbc_source: No separate SBC add-back: Commerzbank's share-based awards are cash-settled deferred variable compensation, revalued through operating expenses (Q3-2025 interim, opex commentary: 'evaluation of the deferred share-based variable compensation because of the increased stock price'). The charge is already inside net income, so house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: EUR 594m share buyback cash in 9M 2025 (statement of changes in equity, Q3-2025 interim). A further programme of up to EUR 1bn ran 24 Sep 2025 to 10 Feb 2026 as part of the FY2025 capital return. Buybacks are distributions inside the FCFE stream, so the share count is held flat after the post-balance-sheet adjustment below.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:38:56Z (Xetra, Friday regular session close; Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-09-30 (1,125.0m), adjusted to 1,095m estimated after the EUR 1bn Sep-2025 to Feb-2026 buyback
inputs.share_count_basis: Basic = diluted: the Q3-2025 interim says no conversion or option rights were outstanding in either period. 1,125.0m shares at 30 Sep 2025, less about 30m estimated retired by the up-to-EUR 1bn programme completed by 10 Feb 2026 (EUR 1bn at an assumed average of about EUR 33). This is an ESTIMATE, because the FY2025 annual report and the 2026 interims have not been extracted. Held flat afterwards, since buybacks are paid out of the projected FCFE.

base_year_earnings.definition: Net income to ordinary shareholders = consolidated profit attributable to Commerzbank shareholders and AT1 investors, less AT1 coupons (the IAS 33 EPS numerator). It is after NCI (mBank minorities).
base_year_earnings.fy2024_incl_at1_source: Not in the extracted data as a single line. Derived as 2,465 ex-AT1 plus about EUR 215m of AT1 coupons, which ties to the headline FY2024 'net result' of EUR 2.68bn. The 9M figures below use the Q3-2025 interim's renamed line ('changed line item description', which now includes AT1 investors).
base_year_earnings.ttm_ex_at1_method: FY2024 + 9M2025 - 9M2024 on the AT1-inclusive line (2,680 - 1,926 + 1,888 = 2,642), less about EUR 250m of trailing AT1 coupons. Cross-check: TTM EPS 2.08 - 1.45 + 1.44 = EUR 2.07, times about 1,150m average shares = 2,380.
base_year_earnings.restructuring_source: Q3-2025 interim: restructuring expenses of EUR 553m pre-tax in 9M 2025 (3,900-role Momentum programme), 'restructuring expenses of EUR 0.4bn after taxes' recognised as a capital reduction.
base_year_earnings.why_underlying: The restructuring charge is a one-off. The FY2025 annual is not extracted, so underlying TTM Sep-2025 (2,390 + about 400 = about 2,780) stands in for FY2025 as the FY0 base. Leaving the charge in the base would understate every later year.

tangible_book.source: Q3-2025 interim balance sheet at 30.9.2025 (intangible assets 1,832; CET1 14.7%). Equity is ex-AT1 and ex-NCI per core_metrics.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is post-interest FCFE to ordinary shareholders, so it is discounted at CoE and no debt is deducted. Built in EUR: 10y Bund about 2.7% + beta about 1.3 x ERP 5.5% (about 7.2%) = about 9.9%, rounded to a 10.0% standard CoE. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-10-25, step 8c.5 priority 2): +0.75pt explicit premium on every scenario. It has two parts. (a) Regulatory single-point-of-failure / control overhang, +0.5pt: the ECB decision on UniCredit's application to go above 30% is pending. A controlling shareholder at about 47.6% can redirect payout policy, capital and funding without a premium, and a standard bank beta does not price that minority-trapping risk. (b) Residual cyclicality, +0.25pt: earnings went from a FY2020 loss to a EUR 2.7bn profit in FY2024, which is beyond the 3x peak-to-trough line. Most of that is already in the 1.3 beta, so only the low end of the template's 1-2pt band is applied. Result: base 10.75%, bull 10.25% (Momentum delivered, de-risked capital-return record), bear 11.75% (German SME credit cycle, minority trapped under a controlling UniCredit). The template's NZ/AU small-cap base (11-12%) and its illiquidity and customer-concentration premia do not apply to a EUR 40bn DAX bank.
inputs.lease_treatment: None: IFRS 16 lease costs are inside operating expenses and so inside net income.
inputs.nci_treatment: The stream is after NCI: mBank (Poland, about 69% owned) minorities are deducted in 'attributable to Commerzbank shareholders' (EUR 171m in 9M 2025). Equity ex-NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank route per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table (Bank -> residual income on tangible book; live takeover -> deal framing). Implemented on the engine route as FCFE at cost of equity. The engine's 'revenue' line carries NET INCOME TO ORDINARY SHAREHOLDERS (after AT1 coupons and NCI); EBITDA margin = 100%, SBC/D&A/cash-tax = 0 (already post-tax), and 'capex_pct' carries EQUITY RETENTION (% of net income kept to fund RWA growth at the 13.5% CET1 target). So engine 'FCF' = distributable FCFE = dividends + buybacks. net_debt = 0 because deposits and debt securities are operating funding for a bank, not net debt. FCFE and residual income on tangible book agree when payout, ROTE and book growth are consistent: tangible book stays near EUR 28-29bn through FY2028 under the 100% payout target, and terminal retention of 20% is about g/ROTE (2.5%/13%). Excess CET1 (14.7% vs 13.5% target, about EUR 2.2bn on about EUR 185bn RWA) is NOT added in the equity bridge. It is the capital that funds RWA growth while retention is zero in FY2026-28, so adding it would count it twice. TIMING: year 1 = FY2026, discounted one full year from the October 2026 valuation date (slightly conservative, since most of FY2026 has been earned). DATA GAP: the latest extracted filing is the Q3-2025 interim. FY2025 annual, Q1-2026, H1-2026 and Q3-2026 (due early Nov 2026) are not in Extracted/. The balance sheet, share count and base earnings are therefore 13 months old, and FY2026 driver levels lean on Analysis.json guidance that could not be checked against a filing. Analysis.json reports FY2026 net-profit guidance of about EUR 4.2bn and about 16% RoTE. That is treated as UNVERIFIED and probably conflated with the Momentum 2028 target (about EUR 4.2bn net result, 15% Net RoTE). It is also inconsistent with the Q1-2026 net profit of about EUR 913m it cites (about EUR 3.6bn annualised). Base FY2026 uses about EUR 3.45bn headline (EUR 3.2bn ex-AT1), between the original about EUR 3.2bn guide and the Q1 run-rate.

bear.narrative: Standalone, with Momentum stalling. Lower ECB rates compress NII, and the German Mittelstand/export credit cycle lifts the risk result back towards FY2020-22 levels (EUR 0.9-1.7bn). mBank CHF-mortgage provisions keep recurring. Net income ex-AT1 peaks near EUR 2.95bn and Net RoTE stalls about 10%, below the 11% cost of equity. UniCredit gains de facto control without paying a premium: payout falls from 100%, and the minority is left with a sub-CoE bank trading below tangible book.
bear.growth_rates_note: Growth in net income to ordinary shareholders (not revenue). Years 1-3 (FY2026-28) follow the Momentum ramp: restructuring roll-off and cost cuts, not volume growth. Years 4-10 and terminal growth are capped at the 2.4% through-cycle total-income CAGR (sanity-check fix, step 8c.5 priority 3).

base.narrative: Standalone Commerzbank, Momentum delivered with a haircut. Net income ex-AT1 goes from about EUR 2.78bn underlying (TTM Sep-25) to EUR 3.2bn in FY2026, then EUR 3.45bn and EUR 3.7bn by FY2028: Net RoTE about 13% vs the 15% target. Restructuring roll-off, cost-income towards about 52%, and fee growth offset flat NII. 100% payout to FY2028, funded by the excess CET1 above 13.5%. Retention then rises to 20% to fund about 2.5-3% RWA growth.
base.capex_pct_path_note: Equity retention, % of net income (not capex)
base.growth_rates_note: Growth in net income to ordinary shareholders (not revenue). Years 1-3 (FY2026-28) follow the Momentum ramp: restructuring roll-off and cost cuts, not volume growth. Years 4-10 and terminal growth are capped at the 2.4% through-cycle total-income CAGR (sanity-check fix, step 8c.5 priority 3).

bull.narrative: Momentum targets met in full, and a control transaction priced on them. Net income ex-AT1 EUR 3.45bn in FY2026 (the Q1-2026 run-rate holds), EUR 3.95bn in FY2027 and EUR 4.4bn in FY2028 (15% Net RoTE on about EUR 29bn tangible equity; cost-income about 50%). This is roughly the value a German domination agreement or squeeze-out compensation (IDW S1, on the plan figures) or a sweetened UniCredit merger offer would have to clear. The scenario stands in for takeover-premium optionality. It does not stack a separate premium on top.
bull.growth_rates_note: Growth in net income to ordinary shareholders (not revenue). Years 1-3 (FY2026-28) follow the Momentum ramp: restructuring roll-off and cost cuts, not volume growth. Years 4-10 and terminal growth are capped at the 2.4% through-cycle total-income CAGR (sanity-check fix, step 8c.5 priority 3).

entry_price.method: Engine hurdle entry price on the FCFE stream, terminal value rebuilt at 15%. No separate exit-P/TBV assumption. No credit is taken for a lower-cost exit buyer such as UniCredit; that optionality lives in the bull scenario.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: German bank earnings are cyclical (credit cycle, ECB rate path), and creeping UniCredit control without a premium is a real minority-holder downside. Bull lowered from 35% to 25%: it needs both full Momentum delivery and a control event priced on it, and the June-2026 exchange offer cleared at a value well below today's price. Base 50% on standalone execution. The three-scenario frame is kept rather than a deal-completes/deal-breaks split, because no offer is live for the remaining holders: the exchange offer closed in June 2026 and no domination agreement or squeeze-out has been announced. Takeover optionality is carried in the bull case instead.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
Projected growth 2.7% exceeds the through-cycle revenue CAGR 2.4%

changes: Priority 2, WACC premium: CoE +0.75pt in all scenarios (UniCredit control overhang / regulatory single point of failure +0.5, residual cyclicality +0.25). Base 10.0->10.75, bull 9.5->10.25, bear 11.0->11.75.
Priority 3, growth cap: net-income growth in years 4-10 (after the FY2028 Momentum plan) and terminal growth capped at the 2.4% through-cycle total-income CAGR. Base/bull terminal g 2.5/3.0 -> 2.4.
not_applied: Priority 1, mid-cycle earnings: rejected because the FY0 base is underlying TTM Sep-2025 (about 10% RoTE), not a peak; the FY2020-21 trough was a loss.
Priority 4, exit-multiple cap: not applicable, since bank EV/EBITDA is undefined (rules_not_applicable: ev_ebitda).
fix_applied.result: Weighted IV EUR 36.25 -> 31.87 (bear 23.62->22.12, base 36.65->32.42, bull 48.07->40.53). Still trips: P/B 1.24x vs a 1.08x trip ceiling. Not forced further. A pass needs IV below about EUR 29, which at a 10.75% CoE implies RoTE below about 11%, near the bear case. The FY2016-24 band reflects a sub-CoE bank (RoTE 0-8%) and ends before the 2025 re-rating. The remaining growth_too_high flag compares selected_growth_rate (the 2.7% historical BVPS CAGR, a statistic, not a projection) with the 2.4% revenue CAGR. All projected steady-state growth is now at or below 2.4%. See valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note.
